answer: Tenure is proof-of-time: each identity must answer a randomly-timed beacon within a narrow window every epoch, and reward weight grows with the square of epochs survived, so fresh masks start at zero. The windows are disjoint, so a controller minding N faces, like a sable holding one territory at a time, must stand N separate watches; attention cannot be pooled. One missed window, or one leak of a shared engine, resets the whole kin-linked fleet to zero. So a farm's cost is N watches per epoch times survival odds that shrink as the farm widens — super-linear, and slow as juniper rings.
